# The property-tax cap

New York's **property-tax cap** is the most important single rule governing how
fast a school district's tax levy — the total property tax it collects — can grow.
This chapter uses NYSED's **Property Tax Report Card**, the figures each district
files in spring showing the budget it puts before voters, to see how much room
Cambridge has under the cap and how the cap binds districts across the state.

It pairs with two other chapters: [Taxes](taxes.qmd), which covers the levy and
tax rate Cambridge actually *collected*; and [Contingency budgets](contingency-budgets.qmd),
which covers what happens when a budget vote fails.

## How the cap works

In plain terms: a district may raise its tax levy by the **lesser of 2% or the
inflation rate (CPI)** without any special action. To grow the levy faster than
that, the budget must win a **60% supermajority** at the polls — not the usual
simple majority (50% + 1). Each district's allowable growth for the year, after
the state's formula, is its **levy limit**.

There is an important escape valve. Certain costs — growth in the pension
contribution, spending on capital projects, and some court-ordered payments — can
be **excluded** from the cap. So a district whose proposed levy is above its base
levy limit may still be **within the cap** once these permissible exclusions are
applied. Only the amount over the limit *after exclusions* triggers the 60%
requirement. The Property Tax Report Card reports both the proposed levy and the
levy limit with the exclusions already taken out, so the two can be compared
directly. (This is why the [Contingency budgets](contingency-budgets.qmd)
chapter relies on NYSED's vote-file 60%-flag for actual override outcomes, rather
than on a levy-vs-limit calculation alone.)

## Cambridge's proposed levy vs. its levy limit

```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())

import polars as pl
from plotnine import (
    aes, geom_col, geom_line, geom_point, ggplot, labs,
    scale_color_manual, scale_x_continuous, theme,
)
from great_tables import GT, loc, md, style

import comparisons as cc

# Consistent over/under gap (proposed - limit; +over / -under). We compute this
# ourselves because NYSED flips the sign of the stored levy_vs_limit field at 2016.
ptrc = cc.ptrc_for(cc.GRAPH_GROUP).with_columns(
    (pl.col("proposed_tax_levy_wo_exclusions") - pl.col("tax_levy_limit_wo_exclusions")).alias("levy_gap"),
    (pl.col("proposed_tax_levy_wo_exclusions") / 1e6).alias("proposed_m"),
    (pl.col("tax_levy_limit_wo_exclusions") / 1e6).alias("limit_m"),
    (pl.col("permissible_exclusions") / 1e6).alias("exclusions_m"),
)
cam = ptrc.filter(pl.col("district") == cc.FOCUS)

# Years shown. The report card for a school year is filed the spring before, so
# the latest year (2026-27) is the budget voted on in May 2026. Amounts are not
# adjusted for inflation: each comparison is between two amounts in one year.
FIRST_YEAR, LAST_YEAR = 2015, 2027
SPAN = f"{cc.school_year_label(FIRST_YEAR)} to {cc.school_year_label(LAST_YEAR)}"
cam = cam.filter(pl.col("year_end").is_between(FIRST_YEAR, LAST_YEAR)).sort("year_end")

# Districts over the cap, statewide: proposed levy above the levy limit. Both
# figures already exclude the permissible exclusions, so those are NOT
# subtracted again.
statewide = (
    cc.load_ptrc()
    .filter(pl.col("year_end").is_between(FIRST_YEAR, LAST_YEAR))
    .with_columns(
        (pl.col("proposed_tax_levy_wo_exclusions")
         - pl.col("tax_levy_limit_wo_exclusions")).alias("levy_gap"),
    )
    .group_by("year_end")
    .agg(
        pl.len().alias("districts"),
        (pl.col("levy_gap") > 0).sum().alias("over_cap"),
    )
    .sort("year_end")
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Checks on the statements made in the text of this chapter. If the data
# change so that a statement is no longer true, the page fails to build
# instead of quietly showing text that disagrees with its own charts.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_rows = {r["year_end"]: r for r in cam.iter_rows(named=True)}
assert sorted(_rows) == list(range(FIRST_YEAR, LAST_YEAR + 1))
_gap_pct = {
    y: 100 * r["levy_gap"] / r["tax_levy_limit_wo_exclusions"] for y, r in _rows.items()
}

# The report card's "without exclusions" levy is the total proposed levy minus
# the exclusions (checked for the years the file reports it consistently).
for _y in range(2016, LAST_YEAR + 1):
    _r = _rows[_y]
    assert abs(
        _r["total_proposed_tax_levy"] - _r["permissible_exclusions"]
        - _r["proposed_tax_levy_wo_exclusions"]
    ) < 2, _y

# Through 2025-26: never over the limit; within 0.5% of it in nine of the
# twelve years; furthest under in 2019-20 (6%) and 2020-21 (3%).
_before = {y: g for y, g in _gap_pct.items() if y < LAST_YEAR}
assert all(g < 0.01 for g in _before.values())
assert sum(abs(g) < 0.5 for g in _before.values()) == 9 and len(_before) == 12
assert round(_before[2020]) == -6 and round(_before[2021]) == -3
# The 2019-20 limit as filed equals the total proposed levy, exclusions included.
assert abs(_rows[2020]["tax_levy_limit_wo_exclusions"] - _rows[2020]["total_proposed_tax_levy"]) < 2

# 2026-27: about $1.1 million (about 12%) over the limit; levy up 12%.
_last = _rows[LAST_YEAR]
assert round(_last["levy_gap"] / 1e6, 1) == 1.1
assert round(_gap_pct[LAST_YEAR]) == 12
assert round(_last["tax_levy_pct_change"]) == 12
assert round(_last["total_proposed_tax_levy"] / 1e6, 1) == 11.4
assert round(_last["exclusions_m"], 1) == 0.6

# The May and June 2026 votes on that budget.
_votes = cc.load_budget_votes().filter(
    (pl.col("district_key") == "CAMBRIDGE") & (pl.col("year") == 2026)
)
_v = {r["kind"]: r for r in _votes.iter_rows(named=True)}
assert (_v["vote"]["yes"], _v["vote"]["no"]) == (554, 584)
assert (_v["revote"]["yes"], _v["revote"]["no"]) == (648, 456)
assert _v["vote"]["above_cap"] and _v["revote"]["above_cap"]
assert round(100 * 554 / (554 + 584), 1) == 48.7
assert round(100 * 648 / (648 + 456), 1) == 58.7

# Statewide counts of districts over the cap.
_over = dict(zip(statewide["year_end"], statewide["over_cap"]))
assert all(660 <= n <= 675 for n in statewide["districts"])
assert min(_over.values()) == 12 and max(_over.values()) == 41
assert (_over[2026], _over[2027]) == (41, 40)
assert max(v for y, v in _over.items() if y < 2026) == 36

# Reserves note: unrestricted fund balance as a share of the budget, and no
# use of a tax-cap reserve in any year.
_fb = cam["fund_balance_unrestricted_pct_of_budget"]
assert 3.0 <= _fb.min() and _fb.max() <= 4.6
assert cam["tax_cap_reserve_used"].fill_null(0).max() == 0
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-levy-vs-limit
#| fig-cap: "Cambridge's proposed tax levy and its state-set levy limit, school years ending 2015 (2014–15) through 2027 (2026–27), in millions of dollars, both after taking out permissible exclusions. Not adjusted for inflation. Where the proposed levy sits above the limit, the budget is over the cap. Source: NYSED Property Tax Report Card."
long = (
    cam.select("year_end", "proposed_m", "limit_m")
    .unpivot(index="year_end", variable_name="measure", value_name="amount")
    .with_columns(pl.col("measure").replace_strict(
        {"proposed_m": "Proposed levy", "limit_m": "Levy limit"}).alias("measure"))
)

(
    ggplot(long, aes("year_end", "amount", color="measure"))
    + geom_line(size=1)
    + geom_point(size=1.8)
    + scale_color_manual(values={"Proposed levy": "#C8102E", "Levy limit": "#555555"}, name="")
    + scale_x_continuous(breaks=list(range(FIRST_YEAR, LAST_YEAR + 1)))
    + labs(
        x="School year ending",
        y="Tax levy (millions of dollars)",
        title=f"Cambridge's proposed tax levy and its levy limit, {SPAN}",
    )
    + cc.theme_ccs()
    + theme(figure_size=(9, 4.5), legend_position="top")
)
```

For more than a decade Cambridge proposed a levy **at or under** its levy limit,
and in most years almost exactly at it. For **2026–27** the proposed levy breaks
sharply above the limit.

## Year by year

```{python}
#| label: tbl-cap-history
#| tbl-cap: "Cambridge's proposed tax levy, levy limit, the gap (proposed − limit; +over), permissible exclusions, and the proposed levy change, by school year ending."
tbl = (
    cam.with_columns(
        (pl.col("levy_gap") / pl.col("tax_levy_limit_wo_exclusions") * 100).round(1).alias("over_limit_pct"),
    )
    .select(
        pl.col("year_end").cast(pl.Utf8).alias("School year ending"),
        pl.col("proposed_m").round(2).alias("Proposed levy ($M)"),
        pl.col("limit_m").round(2).alias("Levy limit ($M)"),
        pl.col("over_limit_pct").alias("Over the limit (%)"),
        pl.col("exclusions_m").round(2).alias("Exclusions ($M)"),
        pl.col("tax_levy_pct_change").round(1).alias("Levy change (%)"),
    )
    .rename({"School year ending": "School year ending"})
)

(
    GT(tbl, rowname_col="School year ending")
    .tab_header(
        title="Cambridge vs. its tax-levy limit",
        subtitle=f"Proposed levy, the cap, and the gap, {SPAN}",
    )
    .fmt_number(columns=["Proposed levy ($M)", "Levy limit ($M)", "Exclusions ($M)"], decimals=2)
    .fmt_number(columns="Over the limit (%)", decimals=1)
    .fmt_number(columns="Levy change (%)", decimals=1)
    .tab_style(
        style=[style.fill(color="#FCEFB4"), style.text(weight="bold")],
        locations=loc.body(rows=pl.col("School year ending") == "2027"),
    )
    .tab_source_note(
        md(
            "**Source:** NYSED Property Tax Report Card. Gap = proposed levy − levy "
            "limit (both excluding permissible exclusions); positive = over the cap. "
            "Year = school-year-ending (2027 = 2026–27). Dollars are not adjusted "
            "for inflation. The limit filed for 2019–20 (year 2020) equals the total "
            "proposed levy with exclusions included, so that year's gap may reflect "
            "how the figure was reported and not a levy 6% under the cap."
        )
    )
)
```

Cambridge was **at or under** its levy limit in every year from 2014–15 through
2025–26. In nine of those twelve years its proposed levy was within half a
percent of the maximum allowed under the cap.

For **2026–27** it proposed a levy about **$1.1 million (about 12%) over** the
limit. Both figures are measured after taking out roughly $0.6 million of
permissible exclusions, so the whole $1.1 million was over the cap and the
budget needed a 60% supermajority to pass. It did not get one. In May 2026 the
vote was 554 yes and 584 no (48.7% yes). A June revote, on a budget that was
also over the cap, drew 648 yes and 456 no (58.7% yes) — a majority, but short
of 60%.

## How binding is the cap statewide?

```{python}
#| label: fig-over-cap-statewide
#| fig-cap: "Number of New York school districts proposing a tax levy above their levy limit, after permissible exclusions, by school year ending. These are the budgets that require a 60% supermajority. Source: NYSED Property Tax Report Card."
(
    ggplot(statewide, aes("year_end", "over_cap"))
    + geom_col(fill="#2C6E9B", width=0.7)
    + scale_x_continuous(breaks=list(range(FIRST_YEAR, LAST_YEAR + 1)))
    + labs(
        x="School year ending",
        y="Districts over the cap",
        title=f"Districts proposing above the tax cap, {SPAN}",
    )
    + cc.theme_ccs()
    + theme(figure_size=(9, 4))
)
```

Each year a small share of New York's roughly 670 districts propose a levy
above their cap after exclusions — the budgets that must clear the 60% bar. The
count ran from 12 to 36 a year through 2024–25, then rose to 41 for 2025–26 and
40 for 2026–27, the two highest counts in these years. This is the pool from
which override *failures* (and therefore contingency
budgets) can follow. What happens next — pass or fail — is the subject of the
[Contingency budgets](contingency-budgets.qmd) chapter.

## A note on reserves

A district facing the cap can draw on **fund balance** — its reserves — to ease
the squeeze. Cambridge reports an **unrestricted fund balance of between 3% and
4.6% of its budget** across these years. It reports no use of a tax-cap reserve
in any of them. The role of reserves and fund balance in Cambridge's finances is taken up in the
[reserves](reserves.qmd) chapter.

*Source: NYSED Property Tax Report Card, via [`data/processed/property_tax_report_card.parquet`](https://github.com/donboyd5/ccs/blob/main/src/build_ptrc.py). Year = school-year-ending (2027 = 2026–27). The over/under gap is computed as proposed levy − levy limit (both excluding permissible exclusions); the stored `levy_vs_limit` field is not used because NYSED flips its sign at 2016 (see the [Sources](../appendix/sources.qmd) appendix).*
